conflicts.fact: The 40-price maize dataset (the anchoring data the sequence builds on) changes between lessons: its values and range differ.
conflicts.versions: Lessons 1 and 2 list prices from 86 to 115 KSh. Lesson 3 gives a range of roughly 86–115 but its teacher model uses KSh 110 and 125, which falls outside that range. Lesson 4 gives only four values (98, 105, 112, 120), with frequencies 16, 12, 8, 4. Lesson 5 uses classes 90–149 with a tail to 140–149. Lesson 6 uses classes starting at 40 with a modal class of 50–59. Lesson 7 uses classes 55–94 with a modal class of 70–74.

conflicts.fact: The mean, median and mode of the maize prices differ between lessons.
conflicts.versions: Lessons 4 and 8 give a mean of KSh 105.10, and Lesson 4 gives a mode of KSh 98. Lesson 8 gives a median of about KSh 103. Lesson 7 gives a mean of about 72.7, a modal class midpoint of 72 and a median of about 73.2.

conflicts.fact: The frequency table figures in Lesson 4 are internally inconsistent and do not match the listed raw data.
conflicts.versions: Frequencies 16, 12, 8, 4 at prices 98, 105, 112, 120 give Σfx = 4204 and a mean of 105.10. The calculation gives 4204/40 = 105.1, but 16×98 + 12×105 + 8×112 + 4×120 = 1568+1260+896+480 = 4204, so the sum is fine. However, the raw list shown has far more than 16 values of 98 and different counts from the stated frequencies. The mode share is 40%, and the 16 of 40 matches that. The stated raw list counts do not match these frequencies.

conflicts.fact: Lesson 5 says the ungrouped table came from Lesson 3 and gives its distribution shape and classes, which conflicts with the Lesson 4 four-value table and the Lesson 3 range.
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 uses the Lesson 3 table grouped in width-10 classes from 90 to 149, with a right-skewed shape and modal class 100–109. Lesson 4 has only four values, 98 to 120. Lesson 3 gives prices from 86 to 115 with many distinct values.

conflicts.fact: Class width used for the grouped maize data.
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 uses widths of 5, 10 and 20 starting at 40. Lesson 5 uses width 10 and then width 15 (85–99, 100–114, and so on). Lesson 7 says 8 classes of width 5 starting at 55.

Lesson 5 says it covers histograms with unequal class widths and frequency density. Lesson 7 says the next lesson will cover histograms with unequal class widths, although Lesson 5 already covered this. Lesson 7's model also lists a frequency polygon, which was never taught. Lesson 4 says the dot-plot will be built in Lesson 6, but Lesson 6 has no dot-plot, and Lesson 3 already did one.

conflicts.fact: The order of mean, median and mode calculation.
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says mean, median and mode were already found for these prices before Lesson 6. Lessons 7 and 8 present the mean, median and mode as being computed for the first time (Lesson 8 for ungrouped data, Lesson 7 for grouped data). Lesson 4 also computed the mean.

conflicts.fact: The explanation of why the family and the neighbour disagree.
conflicts.versions: Lesson 8 says the family's experience included a Rift Valley shortage spike. Lessons 1–2 say both shop at the same stall and give no spike. The dataset has no extreme outlier (Lesson 7 has a maximum of 90–94 versus a centre of 72, and Lesson 4 has 120 versus 98).

Lesson 8's mean (105.10) exceeds its median (103), and it says the mean is inflated by spikes. Lesson 4's mode is 98. Lesson 7 says the mean (72.7) is below the median (73.2), so the mean is not inflated by outliers.
